name: Kamar
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Grierson LSI 1905 wordlist-level notes located; no phonology/stress description found

sources.citation: Dube, S. C. 1951. The Kamar. Lucknow: The Universal Publishers. xxvii+240 pp.
sources.note: Ethnography; no language chapter. Preface says the author acquired 'a working knowledge of their dialect' and that nearly all Kamars are bilingual in Chhattisgarhi; ch. VII calls the present dialect 'a corrupt form of the language of their Aryan invaders' (citing Elwin 1939: 63). Appendix I gives kinship terms 'in Kamar dialect', Appendix IV a glossary. No phonetics, no stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia: 'Kamar language', 'Halbic languages', 'Halbi language', 'People's Linguistic Survey of India'.
sources.note: Kamar language article is a stub citing only Ethnologue and Glottolog; Halbic article has no inline citations; Halbi article never mentions Kamar. PLSI list shows vol. 7 'The Languages of Chhattisgarh' (Hindi and English parts, ed. Chitta Ranjan Kar).

sources.citation: Abidi, Shammi & Anil Virulkar. 2020. Photo Hand Book of Kamar Tribe (PVTG). Raipur: Tribal Research and Training Institute, Chhattisgarh. (Hindi)
sources.note: One paragraph (scanned lines 84-88): the Kamar have their own distinctive 'Kamari boli'; in Nagri-Sihawa it shows Halbi influence, in Mainpur/Devbhog blocks of Gariaband Odia influence, elsewhere Chhattisgarhi influence; original-Kamari-speaking families are declining. No linguistic description.

sources.citation: Trail, Ronald L. (ed.) 1973. Patterns in Clause, Sentence, and Discourse in Selected Languages of India and Nepal, Part I. SIL / ERIC ED087206.
sources.note: Checked only for Kamar: no mention of Kamar/Kamari anywhere in the volume (Halbi chapter is Halbi, not Kamar).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1905. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. VII: Indo-Aryan Family, Southern Group: Specimens of the Marathi Language. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Section 'Kamari or Kawari', pp. 386-388 (+ specimen no. 94).
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Only phonetic remark (p. 387): 'The phonetical system is the same as in Halbi, and closely akin to Chhattisgarhi. Compare kon-jan, some one; bata, share; achhe, is.' Rest of the two-page sketch is nominal/pronominal/verbal morphology plus a mixed-dialect note; the Halbi section of the same volume also has no accent statement (grep 'accent|stress' hits only Konkani/Marathi material).

sources.citation: Kar, Chitta Ranjan (ed.). People's Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. 7: The Languages of Chhattisgarh (Part One Hindi; Part Two English). Bhasha Research and Publication Centre / Orient BlackSwan.
